SubItems.Text: Sizes, colours and the questions buyers will ask
Sell an app or game with access codes

showFullCode.title: Show Complete File
showFullCode.description: Show complete file for code, with bootstrap and error handling included.

error.description: A sentence you can show to a person.

field.description: The form field at fault, when there is one.

detail.description: The upstream service's own message, for debugging.

photo.description: `source=photo`: the product photo, up to 8 MB.

description.description: `source=photo`: a sentence or two about the product. Required if there is no photo.

url.description: `source=link`: a product page, or your own app or game page.

slug.description: The link name you want. If omitted, the AI suggests one.

access_url.description: Where buyers use an access code.

price.description: USD. If omitted, the AI suggests a price.

token.description: The admin token. Shown once; store it.

manageUrl.description: The seller's private manage page (contains the token).

in_gallery.description: Feature the shop at `/gallery` while it's live. Off by default.

options.description: What the buyer picks (physical products only), replacing the current options; `[]` removes them. With options, stock is counted per combination in `option_stock` and the shop's own `stock` is cleared. At most 60 combinations.

option_stock.description: Stock per combination, keyed by its values in option order joined with ` / ` (e.g. `M / Black`). A missing key or `null` means unlimited; `0` is sold out.

facts.description: Answers to the "buyers will ask" questions in `suggestions.missingFacts`. Each becomes a product detail on the page (replacing one with the same label) and drops off the list.

paypal_merchant_id.description: The connected PayPal account (`connectPayPal`). Sales go here when it can receive payments.

account_id.description: The seller account that owns the shop, if it was made while signed in.

option_stock.description: Stock per combination, keyed by its values in option order joined with ` / ` (e.g. `M / Black`). A missing key or `null` means unlimited; `0` is sold out.

photo_blob.description: Image id for `getImage`. The cover photo.

DesignSpec.title: DesignSpec
DesignSpec.description: What Gemini designed. OneThing's templates render it; Gemini never writes HTML.

ShopOption.title: ShopOption
ShopOption.description: Something the buyer picks, such as a size or a colour. The shop still sells one product.

photo.description: Colours: the shop photo (id) that shows this colour. See `matchColorPhotos`.

Suggestions.title: Suggestions
Suggestions.description: What Gemini thinks buyers will want to choose or ask. The seller confirms; nothing is applied on its own.

oneOfAKind.description: A single item (vintage, handmade), so options and stock don't apply.

PayPalStatus.title: PayPalStatus
PayPalStatus.description: What PayPal last said about a connected seller account.

emailConfirmed.description: The seller has confirmed their email with PayPal.

AgentProduct.title: AgentProduct
AgentProduct.description: A live shop as an AI agent sees it. Recommendations have `offers`; everything else has `price` and is bought with `create_order`.

shop.description: The link name, which the MCP tools take as `shop`.

delivery.example: Shipped. PayPal collects the buyer's address at checkout.

options.description: Pass one value per option to `create_order`.

offers.description: Recommendations only. Bought at the retailer.

mcp_server.description: The MCP server to order through (`getAgentProduct` only).

result.description: For `tools/call`: `content` (the answer as JSON text), `structuredContent` (the same object) and `isError`.

Referral.title: Referral
Referral.description: A recommended Channel3 product. Buy links are Channel3-tracked, credited to this shop.

retailer.description: The store with the best offer.

verified.description: Whether PayPal confirmed the delivery's signature.

identifier.description: An email address, or a phone number (spaces, dashes and brackets are ignored; keep a leading +).

phone.description: Digits, with a leading + if one was given.

orderId.description: OneThing's order id; the thank-you page is `/<slug>/thanks?order=<orderId>`.

options.description: The buyer's pick, one value per option, keyed by option name.

clientToken.description: Pass to `createInstance` in the PayPal JavaScript SDK v6.

synced.description: Whether PayPal accepted the tracking number.

url.description: PayPal's onboarding page for this shop.

slug.description: The shop's link name after this change.

Channel.title: Channel
Channel.description: `agent` for orders an AI agent placed through the MCP server.

Delivery.title: Delivery
Delivery.description: For digital products. If omitted, the AI guesses.

result.description: For `tools/call`: `content` (the answer as JSON text), `structuredContent` (the same object) and `isError`.

Kind.title: Kind
Kind.description: `color` shows swatches, and the photo of the picked colour.

fromSeller.description: The seller's description or photo named these values; otherwise they're a guess.

url.description: Public image URL on this site.

ProductType.title: ProductType
ProductType.description: `referral` only for shops created from Channel3.

ships_to.description: Country codes; empty means anywhere PayPal ships.

choice.description: The buyer's pick, one value per option, keyed by option name.

x-admin-token.description: The shop's admin token, returned once by `createShop`. Keep it secret.

Nodes.Title: Quickstart: a live shop in five calls

Nodes.Text:
This walks through the whole loop against the hosted sandbox deployment: create a shop with AI,
publish it, sell one unit through PayPal's sandbox, and ship it. Use `curl` as below, the **Try
It!** button on each endpoint page, or the SDKs (see **SDK Quickstart**).

**Base URL:** `https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com`. All payments are PayPal sandbox; no real
money moves. You need a PayPal sandbox **business** account email (the seller) and a
**personal** account (the buyer), from the
[PayPal developer dashboard](https://developer.paypal.com/dashboard/accounts). See
**Test in the PayPal sandbox** if you don't have them yet.
`createShop` takes a photo, a description or a link. A description alone is enough to start:

curl -X POST https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/api/shops \
  -F source=photo \
  -F "description=Hand-thrown stoneware mug, 12 oz, glazed in ocean blue. Dishwasher safe." \
  -F type=physical \
  -F price=34 \
  -F shipping=6 \
  -F stock=8 \
  -F ship_countries=US,CA \
  -F paypal_email=<your sandbox business email>

Add `-F photo=@mug.jpg` to send a photo; Gemini then reads the product from the picture too.
Gemini takes 15–40 seconds to design the page. The reply:

Keep `token`: it's the shop's **admin token**, it's shown only once, and every seller call needs
it in the `x-admin-token` header. `manageUrl` opens the same shop in the seller's web editor.

curl https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/api/shops/oceanmug \
  -H "x-admin-token: $TOKEN"

`spec` is the page design (headline, palette, layout, FAQ). `suggestions` lists sizes or colours
buyers may want to pick and questions they'll ask that the listing doesn't answer. To change the
design in words, call `refineShopDesign` with an instruction such as "make it feel more premium".

curl -X PATCH https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/api/shops/oceanmug \
  -H "x-admin-token: $TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "status": "live" }'

The shop is now open at `https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/oceanmug`. The same call changes
any setting you send (price, stock, link name), and the rest stay as they are.

Open the shop link in a browser and pay with the sandbox **personal** account, or choose
**Pay with Debit or Credit Card** and use a card from the sandbox credit card generator. You land
on the thank-you page.

Building your own checkout instead of using the shop page? Call `createCheckoutOrder` with the
`slug`, pass the PayPal order `id` it returns to the PayPal JavaScript SDK, and call
`captureCheckoutOrder` once the buyer approves.

curl https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/api/shops/oceanmug/orders \
  -H "x-admin-token: $TOKEN"

The paid order shows `fulfillment_status: to_ship` and the address PayPal collected. Mark it
shipped with its `id`:

curl -X POST https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/api/shops/oceanmug/orders/$ORDER_ID/ship \
  -H "x-admin-token: $TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "carrier": "USPS", "trackingNumber": "9400111899223817502345" }'
The tracking number is pushed to PayPal, so the buyer sees it in their PayPal activity.

- Sell an app or game instead of a physical item: **Sell an app or game with access codes**.
- Let AI shopping agents buy from the shop: **Let AI agents buy**.
- Get every paid and shipped order in Zapier: set `zapier_hook_url` (see **Webhooks**).
OneThing makes a one-product shop from a single input and takes payments with PayPal.

1. **Start.** Call `createShop` with a photo (`source=photo`), a link (`source=link`) or a
   product picked from `searchProducts` (`source=channel3`).
2. **AI draft.** Gemini works out what the product is, whether it's physical, digital or a
   recommendation, how it's delivered, the price, a short link and the page design. The
   response gives you the shop's `slug` and its admin `token`.
3. **Check and go live.** `getShop` shows the guesses. `updateShop` fixes anything that's off.
   Send `status: live` and the shop is open at `https://<host>/<slug>`.
4. **Get paid.** Buyers check out with PayPal. Physical orders arrive with the buyer's
   address; mark them shipped with `markOrderShipped` and PayPal shows the buyer the tracking.
   Digital orders get a private download link, or an access code (see the next guide).

Seller endpoints need the admin token in the `x-admin-token` header. Checkout, downloads and
access-code checks are public.

`signIn` takes an email address or a phone number: the first time creates the account, after that
it signs back in. Call `createShop` with the session cookie it sets and the shop belongs to that
account, so sellers find all their shops at `/account` without keeping each shop's private link.
On the website, sellers can also use **Log in with PayPal**, which records the PayPal account their
sales are paid into and fills it in on their shops.

A shop starts from one photo. `addPhotos` adds more (up to 8 in all) and `setPhotoOrder`
reorders or removes them; the first is the cover. With several photos, the shop page shows a
swipeable gallery, and buyers can open any photo full screen and page through the rest.

`connectPayPal` sends the seller through PayPal's onboarding, after which sales go straight to
their PayPal account; `getPayPalConnection` checks where that stands. A shop can also go live with
just a `paypal_email`.

Nodes.Title: Sizes, colours and the questions buyers will ask

Nodes.Text:
While drafting, Gemini also suggests what buyers will want to choose (sizes, colours with swatches)
and what they'll ask that the listing doesn't say, such as dimensions. They're saved as the shop's
`suggestions` and applied only when the seller confirms: `updateShop` with `options` (and stock per
combination in `option_stock`), and `facts` for the answers, which become product details.
`checkMissingDetails` asks again after an edit.

For colours, `matchColorPhotos` works out which photo shows each one and `setColorPhotos` saves
it, so the shop page switches photo when a buyer picks a colour. Checkout then takes the buyer's
pick as `options`, and the order records it.

Nodes.Text:
A shop made from a store's product page, or from `searchProducts`, is a **recommendation**:
buyers purchase at the retailer through Channel3's tracked links, and the shop earns the
commission. These shops have `product_type: referral` and no PayPal checkout.

OneThing has two kinds of caller: the **seller**, who manages a shop, and everyone else
(buyers, the seller's own app, AI agents), who only use public endpoints.

`createShop` returns an admin token (32 random characters) once. Send it in a header on every
seller call:
x-admin-token: Xq3vT9kLm2…

The token belongs to one shop and never expires. Anyone who has it can change the shop, see its
orders and buyers' addresses, and take it offline, so keep it on a server, not in a web page.

A wrong or missing token answers **404**, the same as a shop that doesn't exist, so a token can't
be used to discover which shops exist.

Lost the token? A shop created while signed in also opens from the seller's `/account` page on
the website.

`signIn` takes an email address or a phone number and sets an `ot_session` cookie (there's no
password or verification, since this deployment is sandbox only). Calling `createShop` with that
cookie makes the shop belong to the account, which lists all of the seller's shops at `/account`.
The cookie doesn't replace the admin token for the API: seller endpoints still need
`x-admin-token`.

On the website, sellers can also use **Log in with PayPal** (`logInWithPayPal`), which signs them
in and records the PayPal account their sales are paid into.
No auth at all:

| Endpoint | Used by |
|---|---|
| `checkLinkName`, `searchProducts` | The create-a-shop form |
| `getPayPalClientToken`, `createCheckoutOrder`, `captureCheckoutOrder` | The shop page's PayPal button |
| `verifyAccessCode` | The seller's own app or game |
| `downloadFile`, `getImage` | Buyers' browsers |
| `getAgentProduct`, `callMcp` | AI shopping agents |

Checkout can't be abused to change a price: the amount always comes from the shop, never from
the request.

- `verifyAccessCode` accepts calls from any website, so a static web game can check codes
  straight from the browser.
- This docs portal's **Try It!** buttons are allowed too.
- Everything else is meant for servers and other non-browser clients. Seller calls in particular
  should come from your server, where the admin token stays private.
Every error is JSON with a sentence you can show to a person:
{ "error": "Photo must be an image under 8 MB.", "field": "photo" }

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `error` | What went wrong, written for the seller or buyer |
| `field` | The request field at fault, when there is one (handy for highlighting a form input) |
| `detail` | The upstream service's own message (Gemini, PayPal), for debugging only |

| Code | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | Something in the request needs fixing, or a step is missing (e.g. going live before uploading the file) | Show `error`; fix and resend |
| 404 | No such shop, or the admin token doesn't match it | Check the slug and `x-admin-token` |
| 409 | Taken or unavailable: a link name in use, a sold-out product or size. From `captureCheckoutOrder`: the buyer hasn't approved yet | Pick another; or keep polling capture |
| 410 | Gone: a download link that's used up or expired, or the last unit sold while the buyer was paying (they aren't charged) | Tell the buyer; nothing to retry |
| 422 | The buyer's card or PayPal funding was declined | Let them try another way to pay |
| 502 | Gemini, PayPal or Channel3 failed | Retry after a few seconds |
| 503 | That service isn't set up on this server | Not retryable |

Calls are safe to repeat where it matters: capturing an order that's already paid answers 200
again, and stock is only taken once per order.

| What | Limit |
|---|---|
| Photo sent to `createShop` | 8 MB |
| Each photo sent to `addPhotos` | 15 MB |
| Photos per shop | 8 |
| Digital file | 25 MB |
| Price | $0.50 – $10,000 (USD) |
| Shipping | $0 – $500 |
| Buyer options | 3 per shop (e.g. size, colour), 12 values each, 60 combinations |
| Download link | 5 downloads within 14 days |
| `refineShopDesign` instruction | 500 characters |
| `searchProducts` | 12 results |
| MCP `search_shops` | 25 results |

- `createShop` takes 15–40 seconds while Gemini designs the page. Hero art is made afterwards:
  poll `getShop` until `hero_status` is `ready` or `failed`.
- Gemini calls (`createShop`, `refineShopDesign`, `checkMissingDetails`, `matchColorPhotos`) can
  answer 502 when the model is busy. Wait a few seconds and send the same request again.

The hosted API at `https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com` runs entirely on PayPal's sandbox:
payments, payouts to sellers and seller onboarding all use test accounts, and no real money moves.
Real cards and real PayPal logins are refused.

1. Sign in to the [PayPal developer dashboard](https://developer.paypal.com/dashboard/accounts).
2. Under **Sandbox → Accounts**, PayPal has already made a **business** account and a
   **personal** account. Open each one to see its email and password.
   - **Business** is the seller: use its email as the shop's `paypal_email`, or connect it.
   - **Personal** is the buyer: log in with it at checkout.
3. To pay by card instead, open **Testing tools → Credit card generator** and use the card it
   makes on the **Pay with Debit or Credit Card** option.
A shop needs somewhere for the money to go before it can go live. Either:

- **Type an email:** `updateShop` with `paypal_email` set to the sandbox business email.
- **Connect PayPal:** `connectPayPal` returns a PayPal onboarding link. Open it, sign in with a
  sandbox business account and agree; PayPal sends you back to the shop's manage page.
  `getPayPalConnection` then reports `receivable` and `emailConfirmed`.

After a sale, the payment shows up in that sandbox business account at
[sandbox.paypal.com](https://www.sandbox.paypal.com).

| Try | How |
|---|---|
| Physical product | Pay, then `listOrders` shows the PayPal shipping address; `markOrderShipped` adds tracking |
| Digital file | `uploadDigitalFile` before going live; the thank-you page has the download link |
| Access code | `delivery: access_code` and `access_url`; check the code with `verifyAccessCode` |
| Sizes and colours | Set `options` with `updateShop`; pass the buyer's pick to `createCheckoutOrder` |
| Sold out | Set `stock: 1`, buy it, then try again: checkout answers 409 |
| AI agent | Call `create_order` on the MCP server, open `approve_url`, pay as the buyer, then `get_order` |

The API runs on `http://localhost:3000` (the **local** environment in the SDKs). One catch:
PayPal won't issue a client token for `localhost`, so the shop page doesn't show the PayPal
button there. Test checkout on the hosted deployment, or locally through the MCP server's
`create_order`, whose `approve_url` opens PayPal's own payment page.

OneThing turns a photo, a link or a picked product into a live one-product shop that takes
PayPal payments, or a recommendation page that earns referral commissions through Channel3.
**How a shop is made**

1. `createShop`: start from a photo, a link, or a Channel3 product. Gemini guesses what it
   is, how it's delivered, the price, a short link and the page design. You get back the
   shop's link name and an **admin token**.
2. `updateShop`: correct anything the AI guessed, then set `status: live`.
3. Buyers pay on `https://<host>/<slug>` with PayPal. Sellers read orders and ship them.

**Auth.** Seller endpoints take the shop's admin token in the `x-admin-token` header. Buyer
endpoints (checkout, access-code verification, downloads) are public.

**Access codes.** A digital product can unlock an app or game instead of shipping a file.
Each paid order gets a code such as `K7QF-M2XP-9HTD`; your app calls `verifyAccessCode`
before unlocking. Raptor Rush on miriogames.com is a live example.

**Agent-ready.** Every live shop is also published for AI shopping agents: product JSON at
`getAgentProduct`, and an MCP server at `/api/mcp` with `search_shops`, `get_product`,
`create_order` and `get_order`. An agent can find and order, but the buyer still approves
every payment at PayPal.
All money moves through PayPal (sandbox in this deployment). OneThing never holds card data.

Nodes.Title: Sell an app or game with access codes

Nodes.Text:
A digital product doesn't have to be a file. Set `delivery: access_code` and `access_url` to
where your app runs; every paid order then gets a unique code like `K7QF-M2XP-9HTD`.

After paying, the buyer lands on the thank-you page with the code and a **Start now** button
that opens `access_url?code=<code>`.
Your app checks the code before unlocking:
{ "valid": true, "product": "Raptor Rush: Browser Edition" }

The endpoint is open to any origin, so a static web game can call it straight from the
browser. It accepts the shop's current and former link names, and codes typed in lower case
or without dashes. Each check is counted (`code_uses` on the order).

**Live example:** [Raptor Rush](https://www.miriogames.com/raptor-rush/play/) on miriogames.com
is sold at [/raptorrush](https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/raptorrush) and unlocks with
this call.

Nodes.SuggestedLinkText: Sell an app or game with access codes

Nodes.Text:
Every live shop is agent-ready. An AI shopping agent can find it, read the product and place an
order, and the buyer approves the payment at PayPal. No agent can spend someone's money on its own.

- **Product JSON:** `getAgentProduct` (`/api/agent/shops/<slug>`) gives price, shipping, delivery,
  availability, sizes and colours, images and FAQ.
- **The shop page:** every shop page carries the same facts as schema.org `Product` JSON-LD, so
  agents that browse rather than call APIs see them too.

Add `https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/api/mcp` to any MCP client as a Streamable HTTP server.
For Claude Code:
claude mcp add --transport http onething https://one-thing-ash0.onrender.com/api/mcp
It has four tools:

1. `search_shops` finds live shops by keywords.
2. `get_product` describes one, including any `options` the buyer must pick.
3. `create_order` puts one unit on order and returns `approve_url`. Nothing is charged yet.
4. `get_order` reports `awaiting_buyer_approval` until the buyer pays at `approve_url`, then
   `paid` with the receipt link (download link or access code for digital products).

A sold-out size or an unknown shop comes back as a tool error the model can read, so it can pick
something else. The seller sees these orders in `listOrders` with `channel: agent`.

Nodes.Title: Create Shop
Nodes.Name: create_shop
Nodes.Description:
Starts a draft shop from one of three sources. Gemini designs the page and guesses the
setup; check it with `getShop`, adjust with `updateShop`, then go live.

Sent with a session cookie from `signIn`, the shop belongs to that account, which also
becomes its seller email (and PayPal email, after Log in with PayPal) unless you give one.

- `source=photo`: a `photo` and/or a `description` of your own product.
- `source=link`: a `url`. If Channel3 recognises it as a store's product page, the shop
  becomes a recommendation (`product_type: referral`); otherwise the page is read and you
  sell the product yourself with PayPal.
- `source=channel3`: a `productId` from `searchProducts` (a recommendation).

Takes 15–40 seconds. Hero art, if available, is generated afterwards (`hero_status`).

Nodes.Title: Update Shop
Nodes.Name: update_shop
Nodes.Description:
Changes only the fields you send. Renaming `slug` keeps the old link working (it
redirects). Set `status: live` to publish; a digital product needs its file (or, for
access codes, `access_url`) first.

Parameters.Name: slug
Parameters.Description: The shop's link name (current or former).

Fields.Name: product_type
Fields.Description: `referral` only for shops created from Channel3.

Fields.Name: stock
Fields.Description: **Constraints**: `>= 0`

Fields.Name: in_gallery
Fields.Description: Feature the shop at `/gallery` while it's live. Off by default.

Fields.Name: options
Fields.Description:
What the buyer picks (physical products only), replacing the current options; `[]` removes them. With options, stock is counted per combination in `option_stock` and the shop's own `stock` is cleared. At most 60 combinations.

**Constraints**: *Maximum Items*: `3`

Fields.Name: option_stock
Fields.Description:
Stock per combination, keyed by its values in option order joined with ` / ` (e.g. `M / Black`). A missing key or `null` means unlimited; `0` is sold out.

**Constraints**: `>= 0`

Fields.Name: facts
Fields.Description:
Answers to the "buyers will ask" questions in `suggestions.missingFacts`. Each becomes a product detail on the page (replacing one with the same label) and drops off the list.

**Constraints**: *Maximum Items*: `5`

Nodes.Title: Call Mcp
Nodes.Name: call_mcp
Nodes.Description:
A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server, so agents such as
Claude can shop here. Add `https://<host>/api/mcp` to an MCP client as a Streamable HTTP
server. It's stateless: each POST carries one JSON-RPC 2.0 message (or a batch) and gets a
plain JSON reply, with no session and no event stream.

Methods: `initialize`, `ping`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`. Tools:

| Tool | Arguments | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `search_shops` | `query?`, `limit?` (1–25) | Live gallery shops whose name or headline has every word |
| `get_product` | `shop` | The same object as `getAgentProduct` |
| `create_order` | `shop`, `options?` | One unit on order; returns `order_id` and `approve_url` |
| `get_order` | `order_id` | `awaiting_buyer_approval` or `paid`, with the receipt link once paid |

**The buyer always approves.** `create_order` charges nothing: the agent gives the buyer
`approve_url`, they pay at PayPal, and the agent polls `get_order`. Orders made this way
show `channel: agent` in `listOrders`.

Tool errors (an unknown shop, a sold-out size) come back as results with `isError: true`,
so the model can read them and try something else.

Nodes.Text: The SDK client can also be initialized directly from environment variables using the `from_environment()` class method. This allows the SDK to automatically read configuration values from the runtime environment or a .env file.
Example

from onethingapi.onethingapi_client import OnethingapiClient

# Specify the path to your .env file if it’s located outside the project’s root directory.
client = OnethingapiClient.from_environment(dotenv_path='/path/to/.env')
You can also specify a path to a `.env` file by passing it to the `from_environment()` method:

The same method can accept keyword arguments to override any values read from the environment, and the arguments to override values should follow the same approach as code-based client initialization.

from onethingapi.onethingapi_client import OnethingapiClient

client = OnethingapiClient.from_environment(
    dotenv_path='/path/to/.env',
    timeout=0,  # overrides timeout from environment variable
)
Values provided through arguments take precedence over those defined in environment variables.
